correctness.rationale: For all finite m>=2, with s<t in interval I, fixed nonzero b, A(y)=A0+yA1 real SPD and independent exact snapshots us=A(s)^-1 b, ut=A(t)^-1 b, the Gram G(y)=U^T A(y)U is SPD. Let a=b^T us, d=b^T ut; strict Cauchy-Schwarz in A(s) and A(t) gives Ks=a ut^T A(s)ut-d^2>0 and Kt=d us^T A(t)us-a^2>0. Because A(y)=alpha A(s)+beta A(t), alpha=(t-y)/(t-s), beta=(y-s)/(t-s), the reduced entries are G11=alpha*a+beta*us^T A(t)us, G12=alpha*d+beta*a, G22=alpha*ut^T A(s)ut+beta*d. Cramer's rule yields det(G)c_s=alpha Ks and det(G)c_t=beta Kt, thus nonnegative coefficients iff y in [s,t]∩I; no convex-hull sum-to-one assertion. The rational diagonal m=3 witness with A(y)=I+y diag(1/10,1/2,9/10), b=(1,3,10), s=0,t=1/2,y=-9/10 has exact projected first component -140484100/176978669, although A(y)^-1 b=(100/91,60/11,1000/19)>0 and both snapshots positive; independent exact rational calculation reproduced the determinant 404522672/165571875 and c=(523575200,-570826575)/25282667. For m=2 full-span snapshots give exact positive solution, and rank-one Galerkin spaces have positive scalar coefficient when the exact solution at the query parameter is coordinatewise positive; same m=1. No claim outside I, no more than two snapshots, no varying RHS. This is a universal algebraic proof, not inference from sample tests.

value.rationale: The two-exact-snapshot Galerkin method is a natural simplest nontrivial parametric reduced-basis model, while physical coordinatewise nonnegativity is structurally important in diffusion and concentration models. The theorem determines the full parameter interval where the surrogate is automatically in the snapshot positive cone using only coercivity, symmetry, affine dependence and fixed load, and distinguishes cone membership from convex combination. The minimal dimension-three diagonal positive-system counterexample identifies a sharp and realistic extrapolation obstruction even when the full solution stays strictly positive, clarifying why error estimates do not guarantee physical sign. This is a motivated exact structural/boundary lemma rather than arbitrary finite numerology; no general higher-rank or nonsymmetric theorem is claimed. The derivation is short 2x2 algebra, but the sharp classification and physical failure witness are independently useful.

limitations: Only exactly two independent snapshots, finite m>=2, affine real symmetric positive definite A(y) on I, and fixed nonzero b; does not extend to POD/nonsymmetric/multisnapshot/varying forcing.

The exact cone membership is for nonnegative coefficients in the two unique snapshot directions, not convex hull; outside [s,t] sign failure of a coefficient does not force physical sign failure for all systems.
245 independently checked finite contexts are corroboration, not a proof of arbitrary-dimension or arbitrary-parameter assertions.
